comments.text:
I'm British and I have experienced only two tremors.The first was in surrey in 1998 and was only noticed because I was on the top floor of a three story building. The effect was a minor vibration through the feet. The second was at my home in north Swansea wales. This was a noticeable movement of my office chair. Having studied geology at school, I estimated that the tremors origin was shallow and came from the area of the Craven Fault zone. As it turned out the UK Geological service  reported the source was indeed in the Craven fault system 12 miles away at a depth of 1.2 miles It was a 3.1 on the Richter scale.
This video is vastly over rated and concentrates on 19th century events where building standards were non existent and journalists over exaggerated news to sell copy (some things don't change) . There have been some events in this century that have been above level three. The cause of these events is not the result of fault stresses, instead the cause is the re-balancing and slow uplift of the Scandinavian shield which is readjusting from the release of weight of ice caused by the  last ice age and as for future events there is insufficient stress to create quakes above 5.2 and it should be remembered that the scale is logarithmic which means tat to have a 6 on the Richter scale the amount of energy required would have to be 10x that of the Harrogate event. There will be no large quake and worst that UK nuclear facilities will receive would stop at a couple of cups of spilled tea - a major disaster indeed!
